rules.name: fails_loudly
rules.instructions: Judge only functions whose body can fail (can throw, return error, parse, call fallible I/O). A function that cannot fail is trivially true; length is not a defect.

criteria.true: Failure surfaces: errors are thrown, returned, or logged with context; nothing silently swallowed.
criteria.false: Failure is swallowed: empty catch, catch-and-continue without logging, error replaced with a default as if nothing happened.

criteria.true: The function does one job; its steps all serve the name. Trivial helpers trivially pass; length alone is not a defect.
criteria.false: The function does unrelated jobs in sequence: parsing + I/O + formatting, or setup + action + teardown of unrelated things.

criteria.true: The exported name says exactly what the implementation does; a reader of only the name would predict the behavior.
criteria.false: Name lies or misleads: name says X, body does X plus surprise side effects, or a term is used with a private meaning.

rules.name: comment_pull
rules.instructions: Judge whether the comment earns its place. When the element has no comment, do not judge.
criteria: Comment restates the code or is noise (// increment i, commented-out code).
Slightly useful: paraphrases code without adding why.
Useful: explains why, constraint, or intent the code cannot show.
Load-bearing: captures a non-obvious contract, pin, or warning that would otherwise be lost.
